country: Multiple/international (image datasets from public sources; not country-specific)
models_evaluated: deep learning image classifier for measles skin lesions

links.outcome: Model performance across annotated subgroups (skin tone, age, body region) in internal and external validation
links.effect: TNRs ranged 79.0% to 92.9% in external datasets; lower TPR for Fitzpatrick type IV (77.8%) and upper extremities (80.0%); lower TNR in children under 5 (67.2%), torso (68.0%), neck (71.7%).
links.quote: Lower true positive rates were observed for images with Fitzpatrick type IV skin tones (77.8%) and lesions on the upper extremities (80.0%).

links.outcome: Generalization performance on external out-of-distribution datasets
links.effect: External validation on four out-of-distribution datasets showed TNRs of 79.0% to 92.9% across subgroups, with lower performance in some subgroups.
links.quote: It demonstrated robust performance across all annotated subgroups, with true negative rates (TNRs) ranging from 79.0% to 92.9% in external datasets.

screen.reason: The study develops and performs retrospective subgroup/external validation of a mobile self-assessment AI tool (deep learning for rash images plus XGBoost risk scoring) for measles screening, but does not test a specific operational deployment practice or safeguard.
